experiment_design.technical_details: This experiment designs a hindcast validation framework to test whether resolving aerosol-GHG interaction uncertainties significantly improves the predictive skill of extreme rainfall intensity in East Asia. The core technical challenge is isolating the impact of aerosol forcing from greenhouse gas (GHG) forcing in climate model outputs. We will utilize CMIP6 model outputs, specifically separating experiments with fixed aerosols vs. varying aerosols, and compare them against high-resolution observational datasets. The 'stopping' feasibility metric is operationalized as the reduction in prediction error margin (RMSE and bias) for extreme precipitation indices (e.g., Rx1day, Rx5day). If updated coupling reduces error by >20%, it supports the hypothesis that model fidelity is a prerequisite for viable mitigation verification; otherwise, it suggests other barriers dominate.

experiment_design.methods: 1. Data Preprocessing: Align CMIP6 model grids to the EA-HPD observational grid using conservative remapping. Calculate extreme rainfall indices (Rx1day, Rx5day) for both model outputs and observations. 2. Scenario Separation: Extract model runs with 'fixed aerosol' and 'varying aerosol' configurations to isolate aerosol-GHG interaction effects. 3. Hindcast Simulation: Run statistical downscaling or bias-correction methods (e.g., Quantile Delta Mapping) on CMIP6 outputs to match observational scales. 4. Uncertainty Quantification: Use ensemble spread from multiple CMIP6 models to quantify structural uncertainty. 5. Skill Assessment: Compare model-predicted extreme rainfall trends against EA-HPD observations. Calculate the reduction in error margins when using models with improved aerosol-GHG coupling representations (proxied by models with higher resolution aerosol modules).
